item.title: Hero bystander, teacher praised for saving lives in school shooting
item.description: The bystander who pursued and killed the Silver Rail Elementary School shooter is thanking first responders and the community for their support.

item.title: Trump looking for new press secretary after Katie Zacharia fired
item.description: Katie Zacharia was ousted as White House press secretary Friday after only five days on the job, sources say. CBS News' Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Teacher saved lives when she tackled gunman during Oregon school shooting, police say
item.description: A teacher saved lives when she tackled the gunman during Thursday's school shooting in Oregon, police say. Three children and a teacher were killed in the attack. CBS News' Elizabeth Campbell and Anna Schecter have more.

item.title: Oregon school shooter ID'd, used shotgun bought by mother, sources say
item.description: The suspect, a former student at the school, fired as many as 15 rounds during the shooting, police said, and another 44 rounds of ammunition were located at the scene.

item.title: Vance calls El-Sayed a "weasel" as Michigan Senate race heats up
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed told Michigan voters the state's U.S. Senate race could go down "as one of the ugliest campaigns in modern history."

item.title: ChatGPT led to man's mental health crisis, lawsuit alleges
item.description: OpenAI's ChatGPT platform violated California law in advising a man on treatment for his mental health struggles, according to a lawsuit.

item.title: An inside look at negotiations to free the Oct. 7 hostages
item.description: One of former President Joe Biden's senior aides is sharing a behind-the-scenes look at negotiations to free hostages taken by Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023, in a new book titled "Brink." Author and former White House national security official Brett McGurk joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle now facing defamation lawsuit from donor who accused her of pay-to-play scheme
item.description: Businessman Eric Deters, a longtime Trump supporter who accused Kimberly Guilfoyle of pressuring him to pay her $100,000 American Express credit card bill in exchange for White House access, has filed a defamation lawsuit against the former U.S. ambassador to Greece. Juliegrace Brufke, founder and Capitol Hill reporter for the Sources Say newsletter, and Oriana González, politics and policy reporter for the Washington Sun, join to discuss.

item.title: Teacher and 5-year-old student killed in Oregon school shooting identified
item.description: Two of the four victims killed in the shooting at an Oregon elementary school on Thursday have been identified as a 25-year-old teacher and a 5-year-old student.

item.title: Breaking down early voting trends in North Carolina, Georgia and Florida
item.description: Early voting data indicates some potentially promising signs for Democrats, particularly in North Carolina and Georgia. VoteHub head of data science Zach Donnini explains.

item.title: DHS Secretary Mullin calls Ilhan Omar probe a "strong case"
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin offered more details Friday on the search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar's home, calling it a "strong case" and saying investigators expect to present it to a grand jury.

item.title: Rep. John Garamendi calls Trump "just disgraceful" over Zelenskyy feud: "He's absolutely wrong"
item.description: European Union leaders wrapped up a summit in Brussels on Friday as tensions between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and President Trump rise. Democratic Rep. John Garamendi of California, who sits on the House Armed Services Committee, joins "The Takeout" to discuss the state of U.S.-Ukraine relations.

item.title: 3 children, 1 teacher killed in Oregon school shooting, police say
item.description: Three children and a teacher were killed, and two others critically wounded, in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon. The suspect was shot and killed by a bystander.

item.title: Officials lay out how Oregon school shooting unfolded and share new details of investigation
item.description: Officials in Bend, Oregon, held a news briefing Friday after a deadly shooting at an elementary school, giving new insight into how the gunman was stopped. Three students and one teacher died. CBS News senior crime reporter Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Trump campaigns in Georgia as Katie Zacharia exits press secretary role after 5 days
item.description: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after just five days on the job. CBS News congressional correspondent is in Dalton, Georgia, where President Trump is rallying for Republicans.

item.title: Bones found in Philadelphia's "house of horrors," sources say
item.description: Bones were discovered outside the so-called "house of horrors" in Philadelphia, but it's unclear whether they are related to the ongoing investigation into Raymond "R.C." Horsch, a suspected serial killer.

item.title: Selma Blair arrested after allegedly biting flight attendant
item.description: Actor Selma Blair was arrested after an incident on board a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to John F. Kennedy International Airport Sunday night.

item.title: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary, "You Can See Everything," premieres
item.description: The new Nathan Fielder documentary on Elizabeth Holmes, "You Can See Everything," is now in theaters. Rebecca Ford, senior Hollywood correspondent for Vanity Fair, joins CBS News to discuss the film.

item.title: Vance says admin. must take action when ICE agents "screw up"
item.description: Vice President JD Vance acknowledged Thursday that there are some federal immigration officers "who really screw up."

item.title: Former U.S. intel official on new book alleging UAP government cover-up
item.description: Jay Stratton, former director of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, has a new book out: "Out of the Shadows: Revealing the Truth About Non-Human Intelligent Life." He joins CBS News to discuss what he knows about UAPs.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Oct. 18, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Republican Sen. Kevin Cramer, Republican Rep. Mike Turner, Democratic Florida Senate nominee Angie Nixon and Democratic Iowa gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand.

item.title: 10/16: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Officials provide update on elementary school shooting in Bend, Oregon; Katie Zacharia fired as White House press secretary after five days.

item.title: New brush fire breaks out in Southern California
item.description: A new brush fire has broken out in the San Clemente area of Southern California, fueled by hot and windy weather. CBS News meteorologist Jessica Burch has the latest forecast.

item.title: AOC transfers $1 million to El-Sayed's Michigan Senate campaign
item.description: Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York has transferred $1 million to Abdul El-Sayed's Senate campaign in Michigan. CBS News political reporter Zak Hudak has more.

item.title: JD Vance defends ICE, but says there's a responsibility to investigate when agents "screw up"
item.description: During a "Things That Matter" town hall with Tony Dokoupil, Vice President JD Vance acknowledged that some ICE agents have made mistakes and faced discipline, but said those cases aren't always advertised.

item.title: iPhone Duo already backordered until 2027 as pre-order sales soar
item.description: Consumer demand for Apple's first foldable phone is strong despite the device's hefty $1,999 price tag.

item.title: U.S. embargo, sanctions on Cuba impacting power, access to medicine
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the campaign is engineered to make the government feel like there are no escape valves, which is how people in Cuba describe feeling.

item.title: Sacha Baron Cohen shares the mission behind his comedy
item.description: Sacha Baron Cohen says the primary objective of his comedy is to "get people to laugh really hard. And smuggled in there is a bit of satire." Watch more of Ariel Levy's interview with Cohen this Sunday on 60 Minutes.

item.title: Oregon mom says she ran to son's school when co-worker heard gunshots
item.description: Kayla and Tyler Major's son was uninjured in the mass shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon. Three children and a teacher were killed, police said.

item.title: Americans are taking trips to Mexico for cosmetic treatments, even as potential risks remain
item.description: CBS California Investigates accompanied a group of women traveling from San Diego to Lipo Tijuana VIP, a medical spa that attracts patients from across the United States.
